lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Babylon, 605 BCE. The young men of Judah had been taken far from home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: King Nebuchadnezzar ordered his best captives trained for royal service. Among them: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

lines.speaker: nebuchadnezzar
lines.text: You will eat from MY royal table — the finest food and wine in all Babylon!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The food was rich. The wine was powerful. And accepting it would have been the easy thing to do.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: I cannot eat the king's food. Not because I'm ungrateful. But because there's one thing I won't give up.

choices.label: Tell the guard directly 🗣️
choices.note: Daniel speaks plainly. The guard is surprised but hears him out.

choices.label: Request a test instead 🌿
choices.note: Daniel proposes ten days of simple food. The guard nervously agrees.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Give us vegetables and water for ten days. Then judge us against the others.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the end of ten days, Daniel and his friends looked healthier than all the young men who ate the king's food.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They didn't make a speech about it. They didn't demand to be noticed. They just held the line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And God gave them knowledge, wisdom, and understanding — more than all the wise men of Babylon.
